subject: [PATCH v5 1/7] mm/memcontrol: flatten try_charge_memcg control flow

2026-08-31.patch_summary: This patch refactors the try_charge_memcg function in the Linux kernel's memory control module to simplify its control flow by separating the logic for memsw and memory page counters into distinct paths.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Acked the patch without raising any concerns or suggestions.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Aug 31, 2026 at 09:37:45AM -0700, Joshua Hahn wrote:
> Refactor try_charge_memcg by flattening the nested memsw/memory
> page_counter operations to separate the logic between the two.
> 
> When page_counter_try_charge is made stock-aware, this flattening makes
> the control flow easier to follow since each page counter now has its
> own success/failure paths.
> 
> No functional changes intended.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com>

Acked-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>

2026-09-04.patch_summary: This patch refactors the try_charge_memcg function in mm/memcontrol.c by flattening nested page counter operations, making the control flow easier to follow and reducing complexity.
